//: Project-scoped Claude Code runtime settings for this repo only (INT-01, REQUIREMENTS.md section 1.4).
This file, not managed-settings.json, is what M1 Story 7 (Issue #7) built. Disclosure of all four
section-1.4 runtime primitives follows, so nobody reads this file and assumes more than it does.
1) permissions.deny (this file, below): ACHIEVABLE at project scope, and set here. BUT it is a
best-effort, host-CLI-enforced control, not a guaranteed block equal to a real security boundary.
Documented non-enforcement history: anthropics/claude-code#18846 ('Bash permissions in
settings.json not enforced - requires custom hook workaround'). It also has no documented coverage
of a subshell wrapper (sh -c "npm publish"), an alternate invocation path not explicitly listed
below, or an argument order this file did not enumerate (e.g. 'git push origin main --force' vs
'git push --force origin main'). .governance.json's guard-hook-enforced blockedCommands remains
the authoritative control for these same commands in this repo (npm/yarn/pnpm publish, destructive
SQL, kubectl namespace deletion) - this file is defense-in-depth only, layered on top of it, never
a substitute for it. Destructive-SQL patterns are not mirrored below: they are normally an argument
to a database CLI (psql/mysql/sqlite3), not the invoked command's own prefix, so a Bash prefix rule
cannot practically cover them without enumerating every client and flag shape - not attempted here
rather than claimed and silently wrong.
2) bypass-mode lockout (permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode): NOT settable from this file.
Claude Code's own settings hierarchy scopes this key to managed-settings.json, deployed outside
any single repo, which this project does not operate. Even there it has an open, confirmed defect:
anthropics/claude-code#44642 ('disableBypassPermissionsMode in managed-settings.json has no effect,
v2.1.92') reports the setting failing to stop --dangerously-skip-permissions in a real deployment.
Not built in this story. Residual gap, tracked for REL-01/REL-02/M7.
3) sideload lockout: NOT settable from this file for the same managed-settings.json-only reason.
Not built in this story. Residual gap, tracked for REL-01/REL-02/M7.
4) version floor (requiredMinimumVersion): NOT settable from this file for the same
managed-settings.json-only reason. Not built in this story. Residual gap, tracked for
REL-01/REL-02/M7.
Net effect: this file closes the achievable slice of INT-01 (permission rules, disclosed honestly as
best-effort) at project scope. It does not and cannot close primitives 2-4; a managed-settings.json
outside this repo is required for those, and is out of scope for M1.

FIRST live-*capable* wiring of this repo's own shipped policy kernel (S2), normalizer
registry (S3), and shell-command detector (S4) to a real Claude Code session. Three
scripts, one purpose each -- but see the ACTIVATION note below before assuming all three
are actually wired into the hooks object today:
hooks/pretooluse-kernel-gate.mjs   -- normalizes a live Bash call and calls the kernel's
decide(); denies on POL-05 (opaque/unresolved) or a
configured deny rule. S7 (2026-09-26): it also
evaluates mcp__<server>__<tool> names through the
tool-class normalizer (class = a marker verb a rule
can match) and reads the loader's rules and posture.
The gate evaluates ONLY Bash and mcp__ names; every
other tool_name is still refused fail-closed (no
filesystem normalizer exists yet -- docs/backlog.md).
ACTIVATION (decided 2026-09-07, docs/decisions.md's "S5 activation deferred" row): this

hooks/sessionstart-tool-enum.mjs   -- SUR-03's real half: classifies the session's

session on this runtime (gap G5) -- this script
only ever writes a side-effect file for the next

hooks/userpromptsubmit-halt-relay.mjs -- reads that halt-state file for the current

prompt if any reason is set -- the real halt point
